slides.label: Cloud route worksheet
slides.source_text: Optional reference · Back to the talk In practice Verify the configured boundary Identify the provider, region and any cross-region inference routing. Confirm the relevant retention, logging and identity settings. Check model availability, quotas, pricing and your organization’s agreement. A cloud brand alone does not establish residency or prevent data from leaving a region.

slides.label: Configuration worksheet
slides.source_text: Optional reference · Back to the talk In practice Record what you are comparing Layer Record before running Model Exact identifier, effort and generation settings. Harness Version, prompts, tools, permissions and retry logic. Routing service Provider selection, fallback behavior and data path. Local runtime Quantization, hardware, context and concurrency. A changed harness can change the result even with the same model.

slides.label: Repeated-run probabilities
slides.source_text: Optional reference · Back to the talk In practice The independence assumption matters If each trial succeeds independently with probability p: P(at least one success in k trials) = 1 − (1 − p)^k P(all k trials succeed) = p^k For p = 0.8 and k = 3: 0.992 versus 0.512. These are mathematical examples, not measured model results. Correlated failures can invalidate the simple model.

slides.label: Local model memory
slides.source_text: Optional reference · Back to the talk In practice Active parameters are not the RAM requirement Stored weights depend on total parameters, representation and quantization. Inference also needs a KV cache, activations, runtime buffers and overhead. Offloading can move weights to CPU memory or disk, trading memory for transfer time. Approximate weight storage: parameters × bits per weight ÷ 8. This is a lower-bound estimate, not a fit guarantee.
